clue.text: Recovering addict's experience in late December course?

definitions.meaning: abrupt total withdrawal from a drug, the sudden stop an addict goes through
a meal of leftover Christmas bird eaten chilled in the days after the 25th

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: sudden drug withdrawal, and leftover festive poultry served chilled as a dish after Christmas.

clue.text: Top books by English writer

parts.note: a top or lid can be called a cap
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A leading volume by an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English writer' reads as one phrase, but English only gives E; Truman Capote was an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was an American novelist, author of In Cold Blood.

clue.text: Preventing limitless private drinking session

indicators.note: without its limits means the word for preventing loses its first and last letters

parts.note: preventing something is blocking it

explanation.surface: Stopping an unlicensed after-hours drink.

explanation.definitionFit: A lock-in is a pub session held after hours behind closed doors for invited regulars.

clue.text: Experimental approach leading to miscarriage of justice?

definitions.meaning: a method of learning by attempts and mistakes
read literally, a mistake made in a court hearing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a method of repeated attempts, and literally a court case that went wrong.

clue.text: Oil platform close to a port

parts.note: an oil platform at sea is a rig

explanation.surface: An oil rig standing just off a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga, capital of Latvia, is a Baltic seaport.

clue.text: A set dinner turning out disastrously might?

definitions.text: A set dinner turning out disastrously might?

indicators.note: a dinner that goes wrong suggests these letters end up in a new, chaotic arrangement

explanation.surface: A formal dinner that goes badly could leave everyone weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out disastrously' rearranges the ten letters of A SET DINNER; the whole clue also describes what such a dinner might do.
explanation.definitionFit: To end in tears is an idiom for finishing badly, as a ruined dinner party might.

clue.text: Elected member for central London, a feeble sort

parts.note: W1 is the postcode of central London, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected member

explanation.surface: A London MP described as a weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is the postcode district covering London's West End; crosswords often read the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a timid, ineffectual person, a weakling.

clue.text: Anti-vice operation's not working

indicators.note: an operation works on something, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A police vice-squad raid is idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' rearranges the letters of ANTI-VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inactive is idle or out of use.

clue.text: Going across meadows is sheer delight

indicators.note: one word stretching over another, so the word for sheer spans the meadows word

parts.note: sheer, as in sheer joy, means pure
a lea is a meadow, poetic for grassland

explanation.surface: Walking over the fields is a total joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going across' puts LEAS inside PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or a source of joy.

clue.text: Unenthusiastically eating cold starter in Chinese city

indicators.note: the starter letter sits in the city name

parts.note: Peking is the old Western name for Beijing

indicators.note: the first letter of the word cold, its opening

explanation.surface: Picking at a cold appetiser in Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' takes C from 'cold', and 'in' places it inside PEKING. 'Starter' looks like a dish but only gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecking at food means eating only small bits without appetite.

clue.text: Poisonous plant finished taking over country area

indicators.note: one word taking in others, holding them inside it

parts.note: something finished is done
GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain

explanation.surface: A toxic weed has finally overrun a rural district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking over' puts GB and A inside DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogbane is a plant with toxic milky sap, once said to poison dogs.

clue.text: Spicy food: rabbit served up in sauce a girl prepared

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the rearranged letters
food prepared is made ready, so these letters are reworked
in a down entry, served up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter, as is to gas

clue.text: Short cut taken to work several times over

parts.note: to trim is to cut
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: A quick trim done at work again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' removes M from TRIM, leaving TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Triply means three times over, a threefold repetition.

clue.text: They won't appreciate first signs of artistic talent in a French painter

indicators.note: the initials sit within the painter's name

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter

indicators.note: the opening letters of each word, its first visible signs

explanation.surface: Some people fail to value a French artist's early promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first signs of' takes A and T, which 'in' places inside INGRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrates are ungrateful people who show no thanks.

clue.text: Popular piece wraps up piano examination

parts.note: in, as in the in thing, means popular

indicators.note: one word enclosing another, as paper wraps a parcel

parts.note: a section is a piece or part
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A well-known musical item concludes a piano exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wraps up' puts P inside SECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspection is a close examination or check.

clue.text: Pagan, note, will be welcomed by head priest always

indicators.note: taken in by another word, received within it

parts.note: nob is old slang for the head

ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A heathen is always greeted by the chief cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' puts N inside NOB; 'head priest' reads as a single title but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan holds no faith in the mainstream religion, an unbeliever.

clue.text: Mum entertains investigators in New York

parts.note: mum as in keep mum means silent, signalled by shush or sh
to entertain is to amuse

explanation.surface: A mother hosts detectives in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the call for silence. 'entertains' looks like a container signal but is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamus is American slang for a private detective.

clue.text: What's half of a very large number? (Novel conundrum)

indicators.note: the first half of the word for a huge number

parts.note: a trillion is a huge number
Emma is a Jane Austen novel

explanation.surface: A riddle about splitting an enormous number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps TRIL from TRILLION. 'Novel' looks like an anagram signal but names Austen's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilemma is a dilemma with three options, a puzzling choice.

clue.text: Shoot racehorse

definitions.meaning: a plant stem growing along the ground and rooting
a horse taking part in a race

explanation.definitionFit: A strawberry plant's creeping stem is a runner, as is a horse entered in a race.

clue.text: Woman locked in cellar

indicators.note: the name is shut up inside the word, like a prisoner in a cellar

explanation.surface: A woman imprisoned in a basement.

clue.text: Arm us when struggling against champion warrior

clue.text: It's typical of trees to provide shelter in which a schoolboy can hide

indicators.note: something hidden is enclosed within another word

parts.note: lee is shelter from the wind
a fag was a junior pupil serving a senior at a British public school

explanation.walkthrough: 'can hide' puts A FAG inside LEE. A fag in British public schools was a younger boy acting as servant to an older one.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage means foliage, which trees characteristically bear.

clue.text: Actor making debut shortly

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a debut is a start

explanation.surface: A performer about to appear for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' removes the last T from START. It looks like 'soon' but means truncated.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a leading performer.

clue.text: Pre-wedding conflict?

definitions.meaning: the period of a betrothal before marriage
